deep.reconstruction:
The page is folio '4' of a computation on the equianharmonic elliptic curve. Read X_5 as X_ζ = C/Γ with Γ = Z[ζ], ζ = exp(2iπ/6): the hexagonal lattice, j = 0, the curve with the most automorphisms. Its automorphism group fixing 0 is μ_6 ≅ Z/6Z.

(1) 2-torsion. The nonzero 2-torsion points are the three points 1/2, ζ/2, ζ²/2 mod Γ. These are the images in X_ζ of the midpoints of the segments [0,s], where s runs over the set S of the six units (vertices of the unit hexagon). Points s/2 and -s/2 agree mod Γ, so this set identifies with S/±1. The group Z/6Z acts transitively on it, and -1 acts trivially since -P = P for 2-torsion. So _2X_ζ∖{0} is a torsor (principal homogeneous space) under (Z/6Z)/±1 ≅ Z/3Z. The generator can be taken as -ζ = exp(4iπ/3), a primitive cube root of unity.

(2) Fixed points of the order-3 subgroup Z/3Z ⊂ Z/6Z acting on X_ζ. These are the x with (1-ω)x ∈ Γ, where ω is a primitive cube root of unity. They form (1-ω)^{-1}Γ/Γ, of cardinality |1-ω|² = 3 ('de rang 3', probably 'de card 3'). Besides 0 they are the images of the barycentres of the six triangles of the central (barycentric) subdivision of the hexagon, i.e. the centroids of the triangles (0, ζ^k, ζ^{k+1}). These six centroids fall into two classes of 3 mod Γ, giving two symmetric points of X_ζ of order 3, exchanged by -1.

Purpose: in 1983 Teichmüller notes this serves the description of the special orbifold points of the modular curve M_{1,1}, or of level-2 structures over it. It identifies the points with extra automorphisms and how Aut(E) acts on torsion and on the 'hexagonal' cell structure of the torus. This is the kind of combinatorial picture (tessellations, Lego of M_{g,n}) Grothendieck used in the Esquisse. The neighbouring pages are unrelated university notices reused as scrap paper.
errors: The example '(1-ζ)/3 etc dans le cas épinglé' is not a fixed point of the order-3 rotation if ζ = exp(2iπ/6) and Γ = Z[ζ]. One has (1-ζ²)(1-ζ)/3 = (1-2ζ)/3 ∉ Γ, and |(1-ζ)/3| = 1/3 is not the circumradius 1/√3. The centroid of the triangle (0,1,ζ) is (1+ζ)/3. So either the transcription misreads '1+ζ', or Grothendieck uses a different pinning/normalisation, or it is a slip.
'de rang 3' should presumably be read as 'of cardinality 3', i.e. the fixed point set {0, two points of order 3}. The statement as reconstructed is correct.

ideas.what: Nonzero 2-torsion of the j=0 elliptic curve is a torsor under Aut(E)/±1 ≅ Z/3Z, identified with S/±1 (midpoints of [0,s]).
ideas.modern_name: Action of the automorphism group μ_6 on E[2] for the CM curve C/Z[ζ_6]; elliptic points of M_{1,1} / X(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th c., theory of complex multiplication and modular curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and its orbifold points but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Fixed points of the order-3 automorphism: 0 and two order-3 points, images of the barycentres of the six triangles of the hexagon's central subdivision.
ideas.modern_name: Fixed points of CM automorphisms; ramification of E → E/μ_3 ≅ P^1 (three branch points)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct (modulo one example) computation of the torsion and fixed-point structure of the hexagonal elliptic curve under its automorphisms. It is preparatory material for the Teichmüller/M_{1,1} study, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'X_5' is almost certainly X_ζ (subscript ζ), the curve C/Z[ζ].
'L'un des pts fixes' should likely read 'L'ensemble des pts fixes', and 'de rang 3' likely 'de card(inal) 3'.
'paquets' is plausible; the sense is 'groups of 3 mutually congruent mod Γ'.
